newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk opposition submit anti-govt censure motion.
newsitem.headline: Turk opposition submit anti-govt censure motion.

text.p: Turkey's opposition parties on Friday submitted a censure motion against the government in a bid to topple the Islamist-led coalition, a senior opposition MP told reporters.
"The motion has been submitted to the parliament speaker," Motherland Party (ANAP) deputy Cumhur Ersumer said.

The censure motion, accusing Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and his cabinet of dividing the country along Moslem-secularist lines, carried the signatures of four of the five opposition parties in parliament.
"The present government, as well as increasing the problems of the country to an unprecedented degree, has dragged our people into fratricidal fighting," the motion said.

Opposition and dissident government MPs have been negotiating for some time to try to bring down the government, which has been attacked by Turkey's secularists, particularly the powerful military, for putting the country's secularist tradition in danger.
The motion would need the support of government MPs to bring down the coalition.
